correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge4\), selected Kneser vertices correspond to edges \(F\) of \(K_n\); every base pair has a disjoint edge in \(F\) exactly when \(\tau(F)\ge3\). Edge-deletion minimality forces \(\tau(F)=3\) and cover-criticality. A self-contained lemma classifies cover-number-two critical graphs as \(K_3\) or \(2K_2\); a high-degree vertex removal leaves only \(K_4\), while the degree-at-most-two cases yield \(3K_2\), \(K_3\sqcup K_2\), or \(C_5\). The support counts are 15, 10, 12, and 1. Exact algebra yields \(a_4^2-a_3a_5=10\binom n5^2(25-3n)\), \(a_5^2>a_4a_6\), \(a_3/a_4=(n-5)/4\), and \(a_5/a_4=6/5\), proving sharp thresholds. The graph-neighborhood checker exhausts 2,131,004 nonempty subsets at \(4\le n\le7\) and the arithmetic checks cover \(4\le n\le80\). Finite checks supplement rather than replace the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Inspected 1993 Kneser paper and the 2023 Kneser k-domination paper: their lower/minimum-set theorems do not imply classification or enumeration of nonminimum inclusion-minimal total dominating sets, nor the two coefficient thresholds. The closest 2025 polynomial paper concerns H-join graph operations with examples of joins, multipartite graphs, corona and windmill graphs; its general reduction to base-graph domination does not evaluate the Kneser pair family. The non-coverage comparison is by mathematical implications, not titles or failed retrieval alone. Independent priority is not claimed.
residual_risks: An earlier classification of edge-critical graphs with vertex-cover number three may exist in alternate terminology; novelty of the underlying templates is not independently certified.

No independent reviewer or exhaustive worldwide priority validation has been performed.

value.rationale: The complete cardinality distribution of inclusion-minimal total dominating sets is a natural combinatorial invariant not recoverable from minimum total-domination numbers alone. Four sharply distinguished graph templates determine it for infinitely many graphs and yield exact persistent breakdowns of log-concavity at order 9 and unimodality at order 10. These are substantial structural and coefficient-shape phenomena motivating broader investigation of minimal-domination polynomials, not arbitrary computations on isolated examples.
